title: Dinnerware Is 'Twixt and 'Tween Casual and Formal Table Settings
text:
Dinnerware Is 'Twixt and 'Tween Casual and Formal Table Settings. This MIKASA ITALIAN COUNTRYSIDE 4-PIECE PLACE SETTING is high in quality, but it's rather thick and heavy for porcelain. Of course, this is a "countryside" pattern, so Mikasa may have intended for it to resemble the humble stoneware more than the elegant porcelain.

(Note: In one place, the Amazon product page description says "crafted from stoneware"; in another place it says "made from quality porcelain". However, the retail box and the actual dinnerware pieces all say "porcelain". My everyday dishes are Heath stoneware seconds, and these feel different, so I'm guessing porcelain.)

The all-white pattern is a raised design formed from vertical bars beneath a narrow scrollwork band that goes all around the edge of each piece. The edges of the design are NOT crisp and cleanly stamped into the porcelain; and my personal preference in this style of dinnerware pattern is for crisp lines. Again, Mikasa may have intended this effect to suggest a rougher, "countryside" appearance.

Nevertheless, this dinnerware is kind of 'twixt and 'tween casual (everyday) and formal (guest) dinnerware. The all-white, raised design is basically elegant; the heavy porcelain emulating stoneware is basically casual. It doesn't really feel right in either setting--the formal design is just "too much" for use in everyday dinnerware; the weight and lack of crisp patterning make it "inelegant" for formal dinnerware.

This line of Mikasa porcelain is microwave safe and dishwasher safe, which is nice. The bowl is large and deep, good for soup or cereal; the cup has a pleasing upright mug shape that doesn't require a saucer; the dinner plate and salad/dessert plate are generously sized. However, because this Mikasa "Italian Countryside" has a split personality, and doesn't seem quite right either for casual or formal table settings, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).
